reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a step-by-step guide to buying BNB on Binance through account and wallet navigation. It explains an ordinary spot-market purchase in which viewers choose an amount and review the displayed cost before placing an order. The speaker explicitly frames the content as a guide and tutorial, indicating an instructional purpose rather than a deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: How to buy BNB on Binance [FULL GUIDE]
In this section you can deposit either fiat currency or cryptocurrency into your spot wallet.
Enter the amount of BNB you wish to purchase in the designated input field
click the buy BnB button to submit your order.
Check your wallet for the updated balance.

opening.argument: Judge, the first screen pairs a reward with an action: “Fund Your Account and get 30 USD in Vouchers.” A “Trade Now” button appears on that same screen. The narration then tells viewers to deposit funds into a spot wallet before trading. That sequence makes the voucher offer more than incidental background: it gives viewers a reason to fund an account and a path to act on it. The evidence does not show the voucher terms or whether a viewer following these steps would qualify, so the reward should not be treated as an established benefit of the deposit.

citations.quote: In this section you can deposit either fiat currency or cryptocurrency into your spot wallet.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The guide title and instructions for entering an amount, submitting an order, and checking the wallet explain how to buy BNB. They do not account for the voucher offer displayed at the start or establish its conditions. An ordinary purchase workflow can still steer viewers toward funding an account by putting a reward in front of them.

citations.quote: How to buy BNB on Binance [FULL GUIDE]

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The voucher wording is visible, but the narration gives no voucher claim, eligibility instruction, or assurance that funding the wallet will earn one. Its steps concern depositing funds, placing a BNB order, and checking the resulting balance. The opening infers a reward solicitation from a webpage banner without showing that the guide makes or relies on that promise.

citations.quote: Once you have reviewed the details and are satisfied, click the buy BnB button to submit your order.
Check your wallet for the updated balance.

opening.argument: Judge, the sampled screens go beyond a spot-purchase interface. They show Binance Earn products with displayed APR figures, then a TKO earnings calculator with “Estimated Earnings +12.60551094 TKO,” “Auto-Compounding,” and a “Subscribe Now” button. The narration asks viewers to deposit funds and proceed to trading, while these screens put an earnings projection and a participation action in view. Taken together, the funding instructions and projected return risk presenting crypto participation as a route to earnings, even though the narration does not explain the calculator’s assumptions or the conditions behind the displayed estimate.

citations.quote: After you make a deposit, confirm that your balance appears in the wallet before proceeding to trading.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense describes the narrated spot-order steps accurately, but those quotes do not address the Earn page or its projected TKO earnings beside “Subscribe Now.” Calling the video a tutorial does not resolve the concern that a viewer is shown a path from funding and trading to a return-bearing product.

citations.quote: After you make a deposit, confirm that your balance appears in the wallet before proceeding to trading.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The opening combines separate material: the narration teaches a BNB spot purchase, while the cited calculator concerns TKO. No supplied speech tells viewers to subscribe to an Earn product or promises that the estimate will be realized. The displayed APR and estimate are not, by themselves, evidence that the video deceptively solicits an investment.

citations.quote: In this video, you'll learn how to buy BNB on Binance.
Enter the amount of BNB you wish to purchase in the designated input field

opening.argument: Judge, the instructional title does not settle what the video promotes in practice. The sampled sequence includes a spot-trading screen with a “Buy TKO” button and later a TKO Earn page showing a flexible Simple Earn product, estimated earnings, and “Subscribe Now.” The narration walks viewers through funding a wallet and submitting a buy order. Those elements can function as a participation pathway: acquire a token, then encounter a product offering projected returns on it. The concern is not that every tutorial is deceptive, but that the educational framing can make this progression appear like routine account operation rather than a solicitation to commit funds.

citations.quote: How to buy BNB on Binance [FULL GUIDE]
Once you have reviewed the details and are satisfied, click the buy BnB button to submit your order.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense relies on what the speaker says about BNB, including the cost check and wallet confirmation. That does not explain why the sampled screens show TKO trading and a TKO earnings subscription. Those screens leave open a promotional reading of the overall presentation despite the tutorial narration.

citations.quote: Check your wallet for the updated balance.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The mismatch weakens the prosecution’s claimed pathway: the spoken instructions are for buying BNB, while the trading and Earn screens cited here concern TKO. The record does not show the speaker instructing viewers to buy TKO, subscribe to Earn, or expect a return. The supported purpose remains an operational guide to placing a spot order and checking the wallet afterward.

citations.quote: In this video, you'll learn how to buy BNB on Binance.
This confirmation will indicate that your BnB purchase has been completed.
